```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
run <- requireNamespace("BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("motifmatchr", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = run)
options(log_message.verbose = FALSE)
```

multiCSN fits three regression layers on paired single-cell RNA and chromatin
data, transcription factor (TF) to gene, TF to region and region to gene, and
links them into factorized TF-region-gene chains. This vignette runs the
workflow on simulated data.

## Input

The input is a Seurat object with a normalized RNA assay, a TF-IDF normalized
chromatin assay with a gene annotation, and a metadata column with the cell
groups to fit.

```{r input}
library(multiCSN)
set.seed(1)
simulated <- simulate_csn_data(n_cells = 300, n_genes = 80, n_tfs = 30, n_peaks = 3000)
object <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(create_seurat_object(simulated, variable_features = 50)))
object <- Signac::RunTFIDF(object, assay = "ATAC", verbose = FALSE)
object
```

## Candidate catalogue

`prepare_candidates()` keeps every RNA gene as a candidate target, scans the
peaks for motifs with the bundled `motifs` and `motif2tf` resources and
records the TFs with a motif.

```{r candidates}
genome <- BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38::BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38
object <- prepare_candidates(object, group.by = "celltype", genome = genome, verbose = FALSE)
get_attribute(object, attribute = "celltypes")
length(get_attribute(object, attribute = "tfs"))
```

## Fitting

Fit one network per cell group. `preset = "state"` suits cell states sharing
one normalization; `preset = "timepoint"` re-normalizes the group and requires
targets and TFs to be detected in 20 cells. Any argument you pass overrides
the preset.

```{r fit}
output <- file.path(tempdir(), "celltype_1")
fit <- fit_layered_network(
  object,
  cell_group = "celltype_1",
  preset = "state",
  upstream = 5e7,
  output_dir = output,
  verbose = FALSE
)
fit$summary
```

With `output_dir`, the tables are written only after the fit completes, and a
re-run never overwrites an existing result. Each table has signed ordinal
weights in `weight`.

## Reading results

```{r read}
validate_network_endpoints(output)
networks <- read_network_endpoints(output)
names(networks)
head(networks$`TF-gene`)
```

## Comparing states

```{r compare}
other <- fit_layered_network(
  object, cell_group = "celltype_2", preset = "state", upstream = 5e7, verbose = FALSE
)
first <- read_network_endpoints(output, "TF-gene", direction = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)
second <- data.frame(
  regulator = other$tf_gene$regulator,
  target = other$tf_gene$target,
  direction = sign(other$tf_gene$weight)
)
transitions <- classify_edge_transitions(first, second, from = "celltype_1", to = "celltype_2")
table(transitions$topology_class)
```
